repo_notes.content: SCOPE — what this repository is and is not. telegram-kb crawls public Telegram channels into a local SQLite index and exposes it to Claude over MCP, with every result citing its t.me post. Several directories hold material that is NOT this project's API and must not be turned into pages describing it. research/ holds investigation notes and reproducible probes, many about third-party behaviour (SwiftPM traits and binary targets, TDLib, GRDB, SwiftSoup, the MCP Swift SDK) rather than this code; cover it as one topic, the project's evidence-gathering practice, and do not document the third-party projects it discusses. reports/ holds drafts of upstream bug reports and their reproduction packages, written to be filed elsewhere. Tests/TelegramKBIngestTests/Fixtures/ and research/fixtures/ are captured Telegram HTML. Spec/url-canonical/corpus-canonical.tsv and Spec/url-canonical/effective-url.tsv are large generated golden files; the substance is Spec/url-canonical/SPEC.md and fixtures.json. Root-level SYNC-*.md and OPEN-QUESTIONS.md files, when present, are transient coordination notes, not documentation.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in precedence order. The direction documents in Sources/TelegramKB/TelegramKB.docc/ outrank README.md and any code comment: Design.md records decisions together with their rejected alternatives and is the most valuable prose in the repository; Roadmap.md is the slice plan (S0–S6, then Phases 2–4); TechDebt.md is the numbered TD-n register, where some entries are marked discharged or superseded and must be presented that way; Research.md is a Verified/Unverified evidence ledger whose distinction must be preserved — never present an Unverified entry as established. REVIEW.md lists review rules derived from real bugs and is a good index of where the code is fragile. evals/golden-queries.md defines the retrieval quality bar (G1–G10) against a real corpus.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: SHAPE AND CONSTRAINTS that any useful page set must convey. One SwiftPM package, two executables over one SQLite store. tgkb (Sources/tgkb) performs ingestion — sync, query, doctor — and owns all network access and credentials. tgkb-mcp (Sources/tgkb-mcp, Sources/TelegramKBMCP) is a read-only stdio MCP server with no network, no credentials and no ban exposure; Scripts/check-invariants.sh asserts its dependency closure is exactly itself, TelegramKBMCP, TelegramKBStore and TelegramKBModel. Library targets: TelegramKBModel (value types, URL canonicaliser, no I/O), TelegramKBStore (GRDB schema, dual FTS5 index — unicode61 with NLTagger lemmas plus trigram — search merge policy, crawl state), TelegramKBIngest (web-preview parser, crawler, channel classifier). The TDLib ingestion target sits behind a SwiftPM trait that is OFF by default. Status: ingestion, search and the CLI are built and tested; the MCP server is the next slice and is currently a placeholder, so describe its tool surface as planned, from Roadmap.md and Design.md. The project indexes Russian and English text, and Russian morphology and ё/е folding are first-class concerns. Licensing is load-bearing: code must never be vendored from Telegram-iOS or Swiftgram's Telegram-iOS fork, both GPLv2.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: WHERE CORRECTNESS LIVES — worth a page of its own. The subtle logic is crawl state, not parsing: Store.CrawlState in Sources/TelegramKBStore/Store.swift decides, as pure functions (since, resumeFrom, afterPage, afterWalk), what a first backfill, a resumed backfill, an incremental sync and a --full refresh may record, so that an interrupted or throttled crawl can never mark history complete or skip posts. WebPreviewSource.crawl in Sources/TelegramKBIngest/WebPreviewSource.swift distinguishes proven exhaustion (reachedEnd) from merely stopping. Design.md sections 'A failed fetch is never exhaustion', 'Crawl state belongs in the database, not beside it' and 'Integrity: ids are dense, posts are not' carry the reasoning, including the concrete failures that shaped it. A second seam is Spec/url-canonical/SPEC.md, a versioned URL canonicalisation contract implemented independently by another project and tested against shared fixtures.
